titulo: Remotion: frame, interpolate, spring, and when to pick React
lead: Remotion does the same thing as HyperFrames in another language: each frame is a React component that receives the frame number. interpolate maps frames to values and spring gives physics to an entrance. In this lesson you render the same idea from lesson 2 in React, read the license, and decide when each engine is worth more.
objetivo: render a Remotion composition with interpolate and spring and choose between Remotion and HyperFrames.

aprende.t: Composition: id, fps, duration in frames, and size
interpolate with clamp and easing; spring with damping
HyperFrames or Remotion: the criteria for choosing

hero_alt: Editing monitor with a smooth animation curve drawn as a graph and a timeline of frames below.

secoes.sub: Tap each piece. Compare with the diagram from lesson 1: it is the same drawing in React.

nos.detalhe: <Composition id="Abertura" durationInFrames={150} fps={30} width={1920} height={1080} />. The duration is in frames: 150 at 30 fps = 5 s. The id is the name the render asks for.
The component receives the frame number and returns the drawing for that frame. Same frame, same drawing.

interpolate(frame, [20, 60], [0, 640]) goes from 0 to 640 between frames 20 and 60; clamp holds the value at the ends; easing changes the curve. spring gives an entrance with spring physics, from 0 to 1.
npx remotion render src/index.tsx Abertura out/abertura.mp4. --concurrency limits how many tabs render together.

secoes.legenda: HyperFrames: time in seconds and GSAP. Remotion: time in frames and React.

secoes.sub: Title with spring, rule, and subtitle with interpolate. The package.json pins remotion 4.0.537 (npm, 10/19/2026).

blocos.conteudo:
K=~/projetos/formacao-cinema-ia-motion-v72/kit
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-motion/a5; rm -rf "$E"; mkdir -p "$E/remotion"
cp -r "$K"/remotion/{package.json,package-lock.json,src} "$E/remotion/"; cd "$E/remotion"
npm ci --no-audit --no-fund > npm.log 2>&1; echo "npm: $?"
npx remotion render src/index.tsx Abertura out/abertura.mp4 --concurrency=2 > render.log 2>&1
echo "render: $?"
python3 "$K/conferir.py" out/abertura.mp4 5 1920x1080; echo "saída: $?"

abas.html:
npm: 0
render: 0
OK: 5,0 s · 1920×1080 · 30 fps · sem áudio
saída: 0

npm ci installs 245 MB into node_modules (measured on this machine). The first render may download the browser that Remotion uses.

secoes.sub: What to read before using it in a company project.

texto: Remotion's LICENSE.md allows free use for individuals, nonprofit organizations, and companies of up to 3 people; above that, the company needs the paid license.
HyperFrames is Apache-2.0: free to use, including commercially.

The Remotion 5.0 migration page mentions a license change (contractors would start counting toward the team). On 10/19/2026, 5.0 hadn't been released and the rule wasn't confirmed: reread LICENSE.md when you update.
A team that already writes React, components reused from an app, data passed through props, video generated inside a React product.
A piece that an agent writes from scratch, with no build; a check with built-in layout and contrast; frame snapshots; local TTS and transcription in the same CLI (lesson 7).

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after you answer.

perguntas.p: durationInFrames={150} at fps={30} gives how many seconds?
perguntas.explica: Duration in frames divided by frames per second: 150 ÷ 30 = 5. In HyperFrames you write data-duration="5" directly.

perguntas.p: What is extrapolateRight: 'clamp' in interpolate for?
opcoes: To hold the value at the end of the range after it finishes.
To make the animation go back to the start when it ends.
To make the render use less memory on each frame.
To make sure the value never goes above the number 1.
perguntas.explica: Without clamp, interpolate keeps following the line: after frame 60 the bar would go past 640 px. The clamp holds the value at the end of the range.

perguntas.p: A 12-person company wants to use Remotion 4 in client videos. What should it do first?
opcoes: Nothing: Remotion is open source and always free.
Read the LICENSE.md: above 3 people it is paid.
Switch to version 5.0, which frees up use for companies.
Use only HyperFrames, because Remotion bans companies.
perguntas.explica: On 4.0.x, Remotion is free for individuals, nonprofits, and companies of up to 3 people; above that, a paid license. 5.0 hadn't been released on 10/19/2026: reread LICENSE.md every time you update.

perguntas.p: When is Remotion usually worth more than HyperFrames?
opcoes: When the agent is going to write the piece from scratch, in plain HTML.
When you need a local voice in the same CLI as the render.
When the piece is a single animated title a few seconds long.
When the team already has React components.
perguntas.explica: Remotion's advantage is the React ecosystem: components, props, and types. For a piece an agent writes from scratch, HyperFrames' HTML has fewer parts that can go wrong.

itens.texto: In Remotion, everything is a function of the frame number: interpolate and spring draw the curve.
Free up to 3 people on 4.0.x; read the LICENSE.md with every update.
React when there is React to reuse; HTML when the agent writes from scratch.
